jobs.occupation: CONSULTANT REGULATORY AFFAIRS Biocides, junior or medior
jobs.description:
Ensus Consulting BV is a consulting and services firm operating at the interface between science, government and industry. We provide tailor-made Regulatory Affairs dossier management services to national and international customers covering all aspects of dossiers related to chemicals legislations including the Biocidal Products Regulation (BPR), Plant Protection Products Regulation (PPPR), etc. In order to further expand our small regulatory affairs team, we are looking for a highly motivated new colleague.
 

After an initial period of training on-the-job, you will soon be expected to work independently. You will support companies in their regulatory challenges related to chemical products, incl. biocides and pesticides. You coordinate and support regulatory dossiers —covering both national and European chemical legislations— from start to finish. The latter includes for example setting up challenging efficacy testing scenarios, discussions with laboratories on analytical testing, dossier creation, etc. Furthermore, you will be able to take part to European discussions on drafting the guidance and commenting on existing guidance documents.
 

While we strongly value the capacity to work independently, it is also essential to cooperate with your colleagues, external partners and experts, authorities and our (inter)national customers.

The ideal candidate should:
 

be a (recent) graduate (Master or PhD level) in a life sciences discipline (chemistry, biology, biosciences, bioengineering, …).
 

be eager to develop expertise in the main aspects involved in dossier preparation: analytical chemistry, microbiology, (eco)toxicology, exposure assessment, risk assessment, modelling, classification and labelling, ...
 

preferably have relevant experience in research projects, through internships or industry trainee programmes. While demonstrated experience in executing regulatory projects (BPR, PPPR, CLP, … ) would be beneficial, it is not strictly required.
 

have the following analytical skills: a keen eye for detail, collecting and analysing data with a critical eye, enjoying solving complex problems.
 

have excellent writing (English) and organisational skills, good interpersonal skills, responsibility and a critical mind.
 

have sound skills in Microsoft Office Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and will become proficient in IUCLID 6, a software application to manage scientific data on chemicals which is used in the implementation of various regulatory programmes, after an on-the-job training.

jobs.occupation: Senior RF/MMW – Analog and Mixed Signal IC Researcher
jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced IC design researcher who can participate actively in the innovation and design of advanced RF/mmw and high speed (Gs/s) integrated circuits in the most advanced CMOS and IIIV technologies.
Apply 
 

Company
 

Imec performs world-leading research in nano-electronics. Imec leverages its scientific knowledge with the innovative power of its global partnerships in ICT, healthcare and energy. Imec delivers industry-relevant technology solutions. In a unique high-tech environment, its international top talent is committed to providing the building blocks for a better life in a sustainable society. Over 5000 expert scientists from over 95 countries shape tomorrow’s world with their research which is typically 5 to 10 years ahead of the market. Imec is headquartered in Leuven (Belgium) and has offices in the Netherlands, Taiwan, US, China, Japan and India. 

The Imec RF/mmWave and High-Speed ADC group in Leuven enjoys a world-class reputation in advanced high speed ADC and in millimeter-wave (mm-wave) RF Designs. In these fields our expertise is in the design of record-breaking high sampling rate ADCs and integrated RF/mm-wave front-ends in advanced CMOS and III-V based technologies. The design group also performs research in the fields of circuit design for advanced (optical) wireline communication, future RF technologies, mm-Wave sensing for life sciences, and mm-Wave imaging. 

The circuit design group is technically mentored by Piet Wambacq and Jan Craninckx and has an established state-of-the-art research reputation that has been confirmed over the years by our extensive presence in top conferences in solid-state circuit design, such as ISSCC, RFIC, ESSCIRC, VLSI and CICC. 

 

As an independent research center, we collaborate closely with top players in both industry and academia, giving our people continuous exposure to both the latest evolutions in industrial challenges and approaches, as well as into the newest emerging academic ideas and paradigms.
 

What you will do
 

We are looking for an experienced IC design researcher who can participate actively in the innovation and design of advanced RF/mm-wave and high speed (Gs/s) integrated circuits in the most advanced CMOS and IIIV technologies. 
 

Your key responsibilities will be: 
 
 

• Research and design of innovative high-speed, low-power RF and analog/mixed-signal integrated circuits in advanced CMOS and IIIV technologies.  

• Drive the bottom-up evolution of these integrated circuits considering the evolution of scaling.  

• Together with the team, bring new ideas and new technical innovations based on your solid technical experience.  

• Take part in technical interactions with external partners and towards new prospects.  

• Publish your state-of-the-art research results in international conferences or journals.  

Who you are
 
 

• You have a PhD degree in the domain of high-speed analog/mixed-signal and RF/mm-wave IC design or equivalent through experience.  

• You have solid design experience, and you have designed in advanced CMOS technologies (28nm, 16nmFF, 5nm).  

• You have experience designing in IIIV technologies.  

• You have a profound understanding of transistor-level circuits.  

• Experience in state-of-the-art high-speed analog/RF circuit design is a strong plus.  

• You are familiar with the various steps and tools in the design and layout of high performant analog and mixed signal circuits  

• You have solid understanding of solid-state devices, analog/RF circuits, up to the system architecture.  

• You have a broad interest in circuit design and are willing to contribute to multiple high speed analog circuit research domains  

• You can work independently yet in close collaboration with experts from other technical fields.  

• You have excellent reporting skills and can present technical results and choices clearly and concisely.  

• You can easily integrate into an international team.  

• Since you will be working in a highly international environment and will be maintaining a good contact with colleagues and co-workers from all over the world, fluency in English is essential.
